problem: Deep RL agents start tabula rasa and are sample inefficient; one-hot goal encodings fix the goal set in advance and carry no notion of similarity between goals, so knowledge cannot be transferred to new goals.
motivation: A lifelong-learning agent should keep extending its capabilities to new goals without retraining from scratch. Pre-trained word embeddings place related objects (e.g. bathtub and shower) close together, and related objects tend to be located in similar places, so a policy for a known goal can guide exploration toward a new one.
key_idea: Encode goals with a pre-trained word embedding and, during epsilon-greedy exploration, sometimes follow the policy of the most cosine-similar already-mastered goal as a temporal abstraction to speed up learning a new goal.
insight: Transfer helps only when the prior goal is semantically close: shower and toilet speed up learning bathtub, while unrelated goals (bed, toaster) cause negative transfer by steering the agent to the wrong room. Word-embedding goals perform about as well as one-hot goals, and training on larger goal sets from scratch is significantly harder, which supports learning small goal sets first and then expanding. Evidence is preliminary, from figures only, averaged over 3 runs.
method: Goal encoding: the goal object name is embedded with a pre-trained spaCy word embedding (300-d, trained on OntoNotes 5, ~20k vectors) instead of a one-hot vector
Architecture: DRQN (recurrent DQN, sequence length 8) on RGB input, with the goal vector concatenated to the visual features
Prior-goal selection: choose the mastered goal w maximizing cosine(M(z), M(w)) to the new goal z in the embedding space

Modified exploration: with probability 1-eps act greedily; with eps*alpha sample an action from the prior goal's policy pi(s, w); with eps*(1-alpha) act randomly (alpha=0.2 in the transfer experiment)
Training setup: eps decayed linearly over 1M steps, replay buffer of 500k, stop at success rate 0.95 over the last 100k steps; the new policy is randomly initialized

setting.backbone: DRQN (recurrent DQN) with a frozen pre-trained spaCy word embedding for goals, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: RL interaction in a custom MiniWorld apartment (3 rooms, 10 objects); word embedding pre-trained on OntoNotes 5 (task-independent)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (e.g. move forward / turn)
setting.privileged: none at test time (the reward uses distance to the goal object during training)

numbers_note: Results are only given as learning-curve figures (goal-vector comparison, goal set sizes, transfer to bathtub); no numeric tables.
results: Word-embedding goals perform comparably to one-hot goals on 4 goals. Using a similar prior goal (shower, then toilet) for the new goal bathtub speeds up learning, while unrelated goals hurt it. All results are preliminary and qualitative.
limitations: Preliminary results on a single small synthetic environment with a single held-out goal and only 3 runs, with no quantitative tables
Objects are abstract colored shapes in fixed positions, and the prior goal selection is a simple argmax cosine similarity with a fixed alpha
Negative transfer when the chosen prior goal is unrelated; no comparison to other transfer baselines or language models
builds_on: Hutsebaut-Buysse et al. 2019 (fast transfer with custom goal embeddings)
compares_to: learning from scratch without prior knowledge
